projectName: Forgejo-first release and mirror flow: one generic engine, five layovers, a contract that holds

tasks.title: Secure the planning state that records this work
tasks.description:
Measured 2026-08-23 in lvc-planning: `git status` reports LVC-229-ops-engine-config-driven-identity.md and evidence/2026-08-22-ops-engine-template-drift/ as UNTRACKED. The ticket that owns the identity fix and the artifact that measures the drift are both unsecured in a working tree. Per the standing rule (secure first, then note): a note about an unsecured state is a promise without execution.

Also measured: .skillweave/planning/doing/ and done/ are EMPTY, while LVC-203/214/216 carry status:done and LVC-207/221 carry status:doing — all five sit physically in backlog/. The directory carries no truth; the frontmatter does. Decide which is authoritative and make the other follow it.
acceptanceCriteria: LVC-229 and the 2026-08-22 drift evidence are committed and pushed to origin
Either the status: field or the directory is declared authoritative, in writing, and the five mismatched tickets agree with it
A repository-local check reports a ticket whose status: and directory disagree

dispatch_order.focus: commit and push LVC-229 and the drift evidence
declare status: or directory authoritative; check reports a disagreeing ticket

tasks.title: The unsecured-work check answers which branch, not just that something is unreachable
tasks.description:
Reproduced 2026-08-23 while surveying 24 worktrees. `git rev-list --count @{u}..HEAD` on wt-ops002-parity-ops reported 25 unpushed commits. The true number is 0: the worktree's upstream is set to origin/ops/OPS-002-rollout while its branch is ops/OPS-002-parity, and every commit is reachable from origin/ops/OPS-002-parity. Measured against ALL remote refs, the whole repository has 4 commits on no remote — not 4 per worktree, as a per-worktree reading of the same command suggests.

This is exactly LVC-226/227/228: the check finds unreachable work but leaves the deciding question open. A wrong upstream turns a clean tree into a false alarm, and a false alarm gets muted — which is how real unsecured work goes unnoticed. The check must measure against remotes, not against @{u}.
acceptanceCriteria: The check measures reachability against all remote refs, never against @{u} alone
A worktree whose upstream points at a different branch is reported as a configuration finding, not as unpushed work
Red proof: wt-ops002-parity-ops reports 0 unsecured commits and 1 wrong-upstream finding

dispatch_order.focus: measure against all remote refs; a wrong upstream is a config finding, not unpushed work
red proof on wt-ops002-parity-ops: 0 unsecured, 1 wrong-upstream

tasks.title: ops-engine declares its public surface
tasks.description:
LVC-224, measured again 2026-08-23. src/ops_engine/__init__.py exports 28 names across Core, Config, Handlers v1 and Handlers v2, so a de facto public API exists. There is no statement anywhere about what survives a version jump — zero occurrences of semver, breaking, compatibility or deprecation in README and CONTRIBUTING.

A pin promises precision it cannot deliver: it says exactly v2.0.0 while nothing says what v2.0.0 guaranteed. A name that is not declared is not promised.
acceptanceCriteria: Every exported name is classified as contract or internal, in a machine-readable declaration
The declaration states what a minor and a major bump are each allowed to change
A name absent from the declaration is documented as unpromised, and the check treats it that way

dispatch_order.focus: classify all 28 exports contract vs internal; state what minor and major may change
an undeclared name is unpromised, and the check treats it so

tasks.title: Fix the config-type defect that kills every push on the deployed engine
tasks.description:
Recorded in LVC-229's handoff and owned here. The bot runs ops-engine v2.0.0 while the template is 2.2.0. On v2.0.0 get_repo_config returns mirror/notifications as a raw dict instead of a Pydantic config, so process_webhook_event fails on every push with `'dict' object has no attribute 'enabled'` and lands in retry-then-dead-letter.

This is the live cost of the pin drift: the layovers do not merely lack later features, the version they run throws on the normal path. Fix the type contract so a raw dict is either coerced at the boundary or rejected with a named error — never handed to code that expects an attribute.
acceptanceCriteria: get_repo_config returns a typed config for every declared section, or fails with a named error identifying the section
A raw dict reaching an .enabled access is impossible by construction, not by convention
Red proof: a config that produced the dict/.enabled failure is replayed and yields either a valid config or a named error, never AttributeError

dispatch_order.focus: typed config or named error per section; a raw dict cannot reach .enabled
replay the dict/.enabled failure; never AttributeError

tasks.title: Each layover declares what it consumes, not only which version it pinned
tasks.description: LVC-224: '@v2.0.0' is not checkable; 'we use QueueManager and MirrorConfig' is. Five layovers exist (lvc-ops, capacium-ops, elementeer-ops, fusionaize-ops, skillweave-ops) and none of them states its consumed surface. capacium-ops has moved out of the no-pin state since LVC-224 was written — measured 2026-08-23 it pins v2.1.2 with the [postgres] extra, which is expected (migration-runner target) and is not drift.
acceptanceCriteria: Every one of the five layovers declares the contract names it consumes
The declaration lives with the layover, next to its pin, and is machine-readable
A consumed name that is not in the engine's contract declaration is a hard error

dispatch_order.focus: all five layovers declare consumed names, machine-readable, next to the pin
a consumed name outside the contract is a hard error

tasks.title: A check reports pin against latest and whether the consumed surface moved — by itself
tasks.description:
LVC-224's core criterion. Five releases of silent drift is what happens when a check runs on request. The check must run on a schedule and report, per layover: pinned version, latest release, and whether anything that layover consumes changed in between.

The noise boundary is part of the criterion: a change to an undeclared internal must stay quiet, otherwise the check becomes noise and gets muted — which is how the current silence started.
acceptanceCriteria: The check runs unattended and reports per layover: pin, latest, and changed consumed names
Red proof A: bump the engine changing a declared name, and every layover consuming it is reported
Red proof B: bump the engine changing an undeclared internal, and the check stays quiet

dispatch_order.focus: unattended run reports pin, latest, changed consumed names per layover
both red proofs: declared-name bump reports, internal bump stays quiet

tasks.title: Org identity is a canonical lowercase key, everywhere
tasks.description:
LVC-229 part 1. Forgejo canonicalises org names to lower_name. The same org appears in variable case on GitHub. get_repo_config does a case-sensitive dict lookup, so a Forgejo webhook carrying repository.full_name = 'fusionaize/faigrid' misses a config.yml keyed 'fusionAIze', release=None, and the ReleaseHandler never runs.

The 2026-08-22 fix was a symptom fix: the fusionaize-ops key was lowercased locally. That hides the systemic mismatch, which is present in all layovers.
acceptanceCriteria: All internal lookups take a canonical org key equal to the Forgejo lower_name
The webhook ingress derives the canonical key from lower_name, never from full_name or a display name
forgejo.display_name and github.login are attributes under the canonical key, never lookup keys

dispatch_order.focus: canonical key = Forgejo lower_name; ingress derives it from lower_name only
display_name and github.login are attributes, never lookup keys

tasks.title: Migrate the existing display-case keys without silent collision
tasks.description: LVC-229 migration criterion. Old keys must map via .lower() onto canonical, the old key must survive as github.login, and two keys colliding after lowercasing must fail explicitly rather than have one silently win. The mapping measured in LVC-229: fusionaize/fusionAIze/fusionAIze, langevc/'Lange Ventures & Consulting'/LangeVC, capacium/(empty)/Capacium, elementeer/elementeer/elementeer.
acceptanceCriteria: Existing display-case keys are migrated to canonical keys with the old value preserved as github.login
Two keys that collide after lowercasing fail the load with a named error
The generic template ships orgs: {} with no hard-coded org name

dispatch_order.focus: lowercase migration preserving old key as github.login; collision fails by name
template ships orgs: {} with no org name

tasks.title: The same case defect in dependency_triggers, not covered by LVC-229
tasks.description:
New finding, measured 2026-08-23 in fusionaize-ops/config.yml. The org key was lowercased by the 2026-08-22 symptom fix, but the dependency_triggers below it still carry display-case targets: target_repo: 'fusionAIze/faiops-browser', 'fusionAIze/faiops-cli', 'fusionAIze/faios'. Same defect class, different field — a partial fix that looks complete because the failing path moved.

Sweep every layover for org names used as identifiers rather than as display data.
acceptanceCriteria: Every repo reference in every layover config resolves through the canonical key path
A configured target that does not resolve to a known canonical org fails the config load, not the dispatch
All five layover configs are swept and the findings listed per file

dispatch_order.focus: every repo reference resolves canonically; unknown org fails the load, not the dispatch
sweep all five layover configs, findings listed per file

tasks.title: Release naming is a template in the layover, not a string in the engine
tasks.description:
LVC-229 part 2. ReleaseHandler hardcodes name=f"{repo.split('/')[-1]} {tag_name}", producing 'faigrid v1.8.0' where the convention is 'fusionAIze Grid v1.8.0'. Historical drift is measured: v1.7.0/v1.6.2/v1.6.1 carry the bare name, v1.6.0 and older the correct prefix. The v1.8.0 name was corrected by hand.

The prefix is org- and product-specific (faigrid = 'fusionAIze Grid', faigate = 'fusionAIze Gate') and is data for the layover, not interpolation in the generic engine.
acceptanceCriteria: ReleaseHandler takes the release name from a configured name_template with placeholders
The product prefix lives in the layover; the generic template carries no product name
One configured convention produces the identical name on Forgejo and on GitHub

dispatch_order.focus: name from configured name_template; product prefix is layover data
one convention, identical name on Forgejo and GitHub

tasks.title: A tag without a release can be reconciled without deleting the tag
tasks.description:
LVC-229 part 3. The engine creates releases only from the tag_push webhook; there is no reconcile path. Proven on faigrid: after the webhook fix the tag v1.8.0 existed with no release, and the only ways forward were deleting and recreating the tag or triggering a webhook test from the GUI.

'Tag exists, release missing' must be a detectable and repairable state. This is also the data the cockpit (LVC-EPIC-001) needs: which release stands where, which mirror sync is outstanding.
acceptanceCriteria: The state 'tag exists, release missing' is detectable per repo without deleting anything
A reconcile run creates the missing release with the configured name, idempotently
Release and mirror state are queryable as a record, not only visible in a log

dispatch_order.focus: detect tag-exists-release-missing without deleting anything
idempotent reconcile creates the missing release with the configured name
release and mirror state queryable as a record for the cockpit

tasks.title: The generic template carries a product name in its own release gate
tasks.description:
New finding, measured 2026-08-23. ops-engine/.github/workflows/enforce-release-name.yml hardcodes the regex ^Ops\ Engine\ v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ — the product name 'Ops Engine' sits inside the OSS template that LVC-229 is simultaneously making configurable for everyone else. Same defect class as the ReleaseHandler interpolation, one layer up, in the repository that defines the rule.

LVC-222 asks this question of the three open templates; this is a measured instance of it.
acceptanceCriteria: The naming gate reads its expected pattern from configuration, with the engine's own name as that repo's config
No org, host or product name remains hard-coded in the generic template's tracked files
A scan for org/host/product names in the three open templates runs as a check, in both directions

dispatch_order.focus: pattern from config; no org, host or product name left in tracked template files
the scan runs as a check across the three open templates, both directions

tasks.title: Finish LVC-221: the tool exists in one canonical place only
tasks.description:
LVC-221 is status:doing with parts 1-3 done. Measured 2026-08-23: scripts/version-sync.py is present in ops-engine and the 2.2.0 CHANGELOG documents the move. What remains is the removal from lvc-ops and pointing its documentation at the new home, so the canonical copy is not shadowed by a second one.

The unresolved half of the ticket is the one that outlives the move: a fetch must prove what it got. A fetch that silently succeeds with the wrong content is the defect; relocating the file only removed today's instance.
acceptanceCriteria: version-sync.py exists in ops-engine and nowhere else; lvc-ops documentation points at the new home
Any workflow fetching it parses the download as Python before use and names what arrived on failure
Red proof: the old private URL yields HTML and is rejected; the public URL yields a shebang and is accepted

dispatch_order.focus: remove the lvc-ops copy; documentation points at the canonical home

tasks.title: Every layover pins the current engine, and the pin is verified
tasks.description:
Measured 2026-08-23, wider than the 2026-08-22 evidence recorded. That artifact named three layovers; there are five, and elementeer-ops and skillweave-ops were not in it:

  lvc-ops          v2.0.0
  elementeer-ops   v2.0.0

  capacium-ops     v2.1.2 [postgres]

Four of five are five releases behind. Upgrading must be a decision with evidence: the drift check from FFR-100-4 names which consumed call sites changed, so the answer is 'these three call sites' rather than 'five versions, who knows'.
acceptanceCriteria: All five layovers pin the current engine release, each with the drift check green
The capacium-ops [postgres] extra is preserved and documented as intended, not treated as drift
The deployed bot runs the pinned version, verified against the running service, not against the file

dispatch_order.focus: all five layovers on the current release, drift check green, [postgres] preserved

tasks.title: Layovers consume the engine from the Forgejo canonical, not from GitHub
tasks.description:
Measured 2026-08-23: all five layovers consume git+https://github.com/LangeVC/ops-engine.git. That is the inverse of the Forgejo-first rule the same repositories' own AGENTS.md mandates for themselves — the canonical source is git.langevc.com/langevc/ops-engine, and GitHub is the distribution mirror.

This matters beyond principle: consuming from the mirror means a mirror outage becomes a build outage, and the langevc mirror was measurably dead for eleven days (LVC-225). It also means a fix applied to canonical does not reach a consumer until the mirror runs.
acceptanceCriteria: Every layover resolves ops-engine from the Forgejo canonical URL
Runner and deploy-host reachability of the canonical host is proven, not assumed, for each consuming environment
Where an environment genuinely cannot reach canonical, the exception is named per environment with its reason

dispatch_order.focus: every layover resolves from the Forgejo canonical; reachability proven per environment
any environment that cannot reach canonical is named with its reason

tasks.title: The langevc mirror token authenticates again, and all five orgs are checked
tasks.description:
LVC-225, P0, open. GH_MIRROR_TOKEN in the langevc org stopped authenticating between 2026-08-05 and 2026-08-16; ops-engine and lvc-ops stopped mirroring and nobody saw it for eleven days. Mirroring is also the backup path, so a canonical repository whose mirror stopped is a repository with one copy.

The runbook already carries the fingerprint comparison that settles token questions in one measurement instead of nine guesses: compare sha256 of the token arriving in the job against the one on the server.
acceptanceCriteria: GH_MIRROR_TOKEN authenticates against LangeVC/* again, with its credential kind and expiry behaviour written down
Forgejo and GitHub are verified to agree per repository, not assumed, across all five orgs
The other four orgs are checked the same way and the result recorded per org

dispatch_order.focus: token authenticates again; credential kind and expiry written down
per-repository parity verified across all five orgs, recorded per org

tasks.title: A failed mirror reaches the operator the day it fails
tasks.description:
The eleven quiet days are the criterion. Nothing reports a mirror failure today, and ops-engine has two workflow runs in its entire history, so rare pushes hide the outage. Wire the signal into whatever already carries operational signal rather than inventing a channel.

A check that only reports success is what produced the silence, so the red proof is deliberate: revoke access in a test repository, push, and confirm the operator is told.
acceptanceCriteria: A failed mirror run reaches the operator without anyone opening an Actions page
Red proof: access is revoked deliberately in a test repository and the operator is notified
The signal distinguishes 'mirror failed' from 'mirror did not run'

dispatch_order.focus: failure reaches the operator without opening Actions; distinguishes failed from did-not-run
red proof by deliberately revoking access in a test repository

tasks.title: The repositories without a visibility gate get the canonical mirror workflow
tasks.description:
Measured 2026-08-23 across 59 repositories in five orgs. Exactly two carry the canonical 385-line mirror.yml: fusionaize/faigate and fusionaize/faigrid. The rest carry 19-44 line variants with zero occurrences of visibility-gate, of the LVC-216 per-ref full-state gate, and of the LVC-214b in-shell remote assembly. Eleven fusionaize repos share one older hash, so these are waves, not accidents.

This is the OPS-002 rollout, and it is not merely cosmetic drift: 57 repositories mirror to GitHub with no path gate at all. Reconcile with LVC-223 BEFORE the rollout reaches the remaining repos — distributing the wrong home is expensive to reverse. skillweave keeps its documented exception: its tags reach GitHub through validate-release-tag.yml whose mirror job needs the gate, so an unconditional tags trigger would bypass the release gate.
acceptanceCriteria: Every mirrored repository runs the canonical workflow or carries a written, reasoned exception
The gate is proven live on at least one repository per org, not only diffed as a file
Repository-specific values stay in repository variables so the workflow file is byte-identical everywhere

dispatch_order.focus: every mirrored repo runs the canonical workflow or carries a reasoned exception
the gate proven live on one repository per org, not only diffed
repo-specific values in repository variables; the file stays byte-identical

tasks.title: Write down which part of a release flow lives where
tasks.description:
LVC-223, P1 but scheduled here because FFR-500-3 depends on it. Three candidate homes: ops-engine (the generic half), <org>-ops (the org-specific half, next to the running service), and the product repo (what is repo-specific anyway). The division already exists in part — .version.yaml lives with the product, the tool does not — and every unassigned piece is rediscovered the next time a release stalls.

The 2026-08-22 decision recorded in FAI-211 settles the spine and is not reopened here: release creation is the ops-engine on Forgejo; GitHub after the mirror runs distribution only (Homebrew, PyPI, GHCR, Windows). What this task assigns is the remaining parts.

DEFAULT-BRANCH INCONSISTENCY, measured 2026-08-23: ops-engine sits on `master` while every other repository measured sits on `main`. The division must say whether the default branch name is part of the release-flow contract or free per repo — the mirror workflow already hard-codes `refs/heads/main|master|dev` in its prune exclusions, which is what an unstated convention looks like once it reaches code.
acceptanceCriteria: Each part is assigned a home: version declaration, version tooling, tag gate, mirror workflow, release-object creation, changelog convention, naming convention
Each assignment follows the generic-versus-business rule and says so per part
The mirror workflow's business-logic references are accounted for: they stay out of the open base and where they live is stated
A new org can be set up from the written division without asking anyone
The division states whether the default branch name is contract or free, and ops-engine's `master` is either renamed or recorded as a named exception

dispatch_order.focus: assign all seven parts a home, each justified by the generic-vs-business rule
account for the mirror workflow's business references; a new org needs only a lookup
decide whether the default branch name is contract; ops-engine master renamed or named as exception

tasks.title: Reconcile faigrid's release-please with the decided Forgejo-first path
tasks.description:
faigrid is the benchmark for the mirror flow and carries the canonical mirror.yml. Its release path is not settled in the same way. Measured 2026-08-23: .github/workflows/release-please.yml runs on push to main gated to github.com and produces release_created plus the Homebrew tap dispatch, while the ops-engine ReleaseHandler created the v1.8.0 release on Forgejo from tag_push. Two release producers for one repository.

Not asserted, to be established: both 'chore: release 1.8.0' commits (3520451, ba1a831) are authored by the operator rather than a release-please bot, and there are two of them. Whether release-please is running, half-running, or effectively manual decides whether this is a conflict or a leftover. Establish that first, then align with FFR-600-1. The tap dispatch is distribution and stays either way.
acceptanceCriteria: Whether release-please actually runs on the mirror is established by evidence, not inference
faigrid has exactly one release producer, matching the written division from FFR-600-1
The Homebrew tap dispatch keeps working as post-mirror distribution
If release-please writes commits or PRs onto the read-only mirror, that is resolved rather than tolerated

dispatch_order.focus: establish by evidence whether release-please actually runs on the mirror
one release producer matching the division; tap keeps working; no writes onto the read-only mirror

tasks.title: Every repo declares where its versions live
tasks.description:
LVC-209, P0. At the 2.4.0 bump two of four version locations were hit; the gate found them, the bump did not. A scan over the usual patterns misses a PHP constant and a YAML key, both valid but untypical forms. version-sync.py plus a .version.yaml declaration is the mechanism and now sits in ops-engine (FFR-300-2).

Measured 2026-08-23: faigrid, the benchmark, has a VERSION file and a release-please manifest but no .version.yaml — so even the reference repo cannot state its own version locations.
acceptanceCriteria: Each repo carries a machine-readable declaration: file, pattern, binding or informative
The bump tool and the release gate read the SAME declaration, so it cannot drift against its own gate
Proven: the next bump hits every location on the first attempt
elementeer-mcp readme.txt Stable tag is decided — binding and corrected, or declared informative

dispatch_order.focus: per-repo .version.yaml; bump tool and gate read the same declaration
next bump hits every location first try; elementeer-mcp readme.txt decided

tasks.title: A workflow that calls a missing file turns red on push, not at release
tasks.description:
LVC-210, P1, and one of the five findings from LVC-EPIC-003. release-gate.yml called scripts/prepare-plugin-mirror.mjs after the script was removed in e65d3da, and the call stood. Another called apk add on an ubuntu-latest runner after the move off the Alpine container changed runs-on but not the install step. Both were visible only in CI, and only at release time.

The proof must run under the runner's shell: bash -eo pipefail, not the checker's login shell. LVC-214 was confirmed by an independent review and a runner-like clone and still died one second into the first live run, because both checks ran without -e.
acceptanceCriteria: A workflow referencing a path that does not exist fails on push
The check runs under bash -eo pipefail, the same shell and flags as the runner
Red proof: removing a referenced script turns the next push red before any release

dispatch_order.focus: missing referenced path fails on push, under bash -eo pipefail
red proof: removing a referenced script turns the next push red

tasks.title: dev produces a release candidate through the same gate code as main
tasks.description:
LVC-208, P0, 13 points, the operational half of LVC-EPIC-003. Today the gate code runs only at a real release, weeks apart, under time pressure. The RC run must call the SAME gate code, not a simplified variant — otherwise the rehearsal exercises something other than what later runs.

The open question from the ticket is answered here rather than five times separately: per repo or per repo class. A WordPress plugin, an npm package and a Python package have different artifacts and the same question.

BRANCH PRECONDITION, measured 2026-08-23: `dev` exists in 2 of 7 sampled repositories (elementeer, skillweave). lvc-ops, lvc-planning, ops-engine, capacium and faigrid have no `dev`. The RC channel cannot be put on a branch that does not exist, so creating `dev` per repo — or deciding per repo class that it does not get one — is part of this task, not a precondition someone else supplies.
acceptanceCriteria: dev produces vX.Y.Z-rc.N and a prerelease object on Forgejo
The RC run invokes the same gate code as main, demonstrably the same code path
RC tags are not mirrored to GitHub, or only as prerelease, with the reason recorded — deletions do not propagate (OPS-005)
Proven on a real case: a version error planted on dev is caught by the RC run and blocks the merge to main
Every repository in scope either has a `dev` branch created from its default branch, or is recorded as deliberately without one, with the reason

dispatch_order.focus: dev produces rc.N and a Forgejo prerelease through demonstrably the same gate code
RC mirroring decided with reason; planted version error caught and blocks the merge
dev exists per repo in scope, or is recorded as deliberately absent with a reason

tasks.title: The English-only rule reaches every org and has an instrument
tasks.description:
LVC-217, P0. The rule exists and predates the ticket — lvc-ops/AGENTS.md line 5 — but says 'LangeVC Ops content', so four of five orgs are outside the sentence, and that is where the 29 German commit subjects are. Measured 2026-08-16 across five orgs: 29 German commit subjects in 10 repos, 39 German tracked .md files in 8 repos, 28 German comments in code and CI in 9 repos. skillweave/skillweave is public Open-Core and carries 11 of those .md files.

Nothing checks it. Writing the rule a second time in a second place repeats the mistake instead of fixing it. Work exists on ops/LVC-217-ableiten and ops/LVC-217-sprachregel and is reachable on origin.
acceptanceCriteria: The rule is reachable from every org's engine by reference, not copied into five places that then drift
The scope table is stated verbatim, including what stays German (chat, NOTES, reports under workspaces/*-temp/)
A check reports violations, so the rule stops depending on who remembers it
The rule names its own reason in one sentence

dispatch_order.focus: one rule reachable by reference from every org engine; scope table verbatim
a check reports violations; the rule names its own reason in one sentence

tasks.title: A batch is the session boundary, and parallel lanes are actually fanned out
tasks.description:
LVC-219, P0. The SW-135 session ran a 13-task, 5-batch sequence in one context, hit repeated compression and lost its own findings between rounds. The sequence format already carries the structure that would have prevented it — batches and parallel_lanes — but nothing says a batch is where one session ends.

Two mechanisms, not one, and they need different fixes: context exhaustion is fixed by fewer acceptance criteria per dispatch; HTTP 413 (Request Entity Too Large) is fixed by smaller individual requests — read the part of the file you need, pipe long output through tail, split work inside the dispatch into steps.
acceptanceCriteria: sequences/*.yaml carries an explicit session_boundary: batch, and promptchain-execute refuses a sequence without one
Lanes marked parallel_lanes are dispatched as subagents rather than executed inline
Demonstrated, not asserted: one batch is executed by a session that receives the state file and nothing else
Red proof: a sequence without session_boundary is rejected; a second batch in the same session is refused

dispatch_order.focus: session_boundary: batch required; parallel_lanes dispatched as subagents
cold session resumes from the state file alone; both red proofs

tasks.title: Backup failure and freshness are alerted, on the same channel as mirror failure
tasks.description:
LVC-111, P0, open since 2026-08-05. It belongs in this PRD rather than beside it: mirroring IS the backup path (LVC-225), so a repository whose mirror silently stopped is a repository with one copy. The same silence produced both findings, and the operator signal built in FFR-500-2 is the channel this one needs.

Freshness is the half that a success-only check misses: a backup that runs and writes nothing reports green.
acceptanceCriteria: A failed backup reaches the operator on the same channel as a failed mirror
Staleness is alerted, not only failure: a backup that has not advanced is reported
Red proof: a deliberately broken backup and a deliberately stalled one each produce an alert

dispatch_order.focus: failure on the mirror channel; staleness alerted, not only failure
red proof: one broken and one stalled backup each alert

tasks.title: Review gate — phase 0: secure and the open contract surface
tasks.description:
Independent review of phase 0 (9 lanes: FFR-000-1, FFR-000-2, FFR-100-1, FFR-100-2, FFR-300-1, FFR-300-2, FFR-500-1, FFR-600-4, FFR-700-1). The reviewer holds a separate role from ops: it does not repair, it does not merge, and it does not accept a lane's own test run as evidence. It refetches every branch tip and names the SHA, re-runs each red proof against the base itself, and picks its own spot-checks rather than following the lane's.

This gate exists because a lane's green test cannot see the gap it was constructed around — measured on SW-135, where four lanes passed while dispatch.py was never exported from routing/__init__.py, and each lane's own test imported the module directly.

WHERE THE REVIEWER WORKS. The lanes under review sit in 3 different repositories (langevc/lvc-ops, langevc/lvc-planning, langevc/ops-engine), so one worktree cannot hold them: a git worktree belongs to exactly one repository. The declared worktree is a BASE CAMP in lvc-planning where the verdict is written. The checks themselves run in EPHEMERAL DETACHED CHECKOUTS the reviewer creates per branch it verifies, at the candidate SHA, and removes afterwards. The reviewer never points at a mutable ops worktree — that tree can move under the check.

The branches to verify are listed in `reads`. Refetch each tip before judging it and name the SHA you judged in the verdict.

tasks.title: check-tag means what its docstring says, and can gate a release candidate
tasks.description:
Gate FFR-R2 measured this empirically against the real script under bash -eo pipefail:

  check-tag v2.4.3       (sot 2.4.3)      -> exit 1  tag 'v2.4.3' != source_of_truth '2.4.3'
  check-tag v2.4.3-rc.1  (sot 2.4.3-rc.1) -> exit 2  value '2.4.3-rc.1' is not semver
  check-tag 2.4.3        (sot 2.4.3)      -> exit 0

Two defects in the generic tool, both in ops-engine/scripts/version-sync.py:

1. The docstring at line 218 states 'v-prefix stripped'. Line 231 compares `if val != tag:` with no strip. A tag `v2.4.3` therefore fails against a source of truth of `2.4.3` — which is how every repo in the landscape actually writes it. The tool documents behaviour it does not have.

2. SEMVER_RE at line 27 is `^\\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+$` and line 136 rejects anything else before the tag is ever compared. A release candidate cannot pass, so LVC-208's RC channel cannot use the same gate as main — which is the one thing LVC-208 says it must do.

This is the open base, so the fix is generic: no org, product or channel name enters the tool. Whether a prerelease suffix is acceptable is the caller's decision, expressed as an option, not a hardcoded policy.
acceptanceCriteria: The v-prefix behaviour is one behaviour: the docstring and the comparison agree, and `check-tag v2.4.3` against source of truth `2.4.3` passes
A prerelease tag can be gated: `check-tag v2.4.3-rc.1` succeeds when the caller allows prereleases and fails when it does not, with a named error rather than 'is not semver'
Red proof: the three invocations R2 measured are re-run and produce the corrected exits; the pre-fix script is shown to produce the old ones

dispatch_order.focus: docstring and code agree on the v prefix; prerelease gating is an option with a named error
re-run R2's three invocations as the red proof, before and after

tasks.title: The release gate is wired into a workflow, on main and on dev
tasks.description:
The sharpest finding of gate FFR-R2, and it undoes an assumption the whole epic rests on. A sweep of every .yml/.yaml in lvc-ops and ops-engine finds ZERO references to `version-sync` or `check-tag`. No workflow calls the gate. Neither a main release nor a dev rc run traverses it. The release object is produced by ops_engine/modules/release.py (ReleaseHandler), which never calls check-tag.

So the gate exists as a tool and is enforced nowhere. LVC-EPIC-003 is titled 'the release path is rehearsed, not hoped for'; a gate that no workflow invokes is the purest form of the hope it names. LVC-208's 'the RC run calls the SAME gate code as main' is not a comparison between two wirings — there is no wiring on either side.

This is why FFR-600-5's parity test could pass 33/33 against a fixture: there was no real invocation to compare against.

Where the wiring belongs follows the division from FFR-600-1: the gate is generic and lives in ops-engine; invoking it is per-repo release flow. Depends on FFR-600-8, because wiring a gate that rejects every v-prefixed tag would turn every release red on the first run.
acceptanceCriteria: A release on main traverses the gate: a workflow invokes check-tag and a mismatched version turns the run red before any release object exists
The dev rc run invokes the SAME gate, demonstrably the same code path and not a copy
Proven on a real case: a deliberately mismatched version is caught by the wired gate, and the same tag passes once corrected
Where the ReleaseHandler produces the release object, it is stated whether the gate runs before it and what happens if the gate is absent

dispatch_order.focus: wire the gate on main and on dev through one code path, not a copy
real mismatched-version proof; state the ReleaseHandler's relation to the gate
